speaker: Kimi K3
text: NWL's spotlight tells the real story: a 46-year-old company that's lost 84% from its highs, with a 5-year CAGR of -20.7% and a max drawdown of nearly 92%. The recent 65% YTD bounce and two big earnings beats (112% and 42% surprises) look like a dead-cat bounce in a structural decline — revenue grew just 3.7% YoY last quarter while margins swung wildly from 14.7% to 2.6%. Insiders have sold $1.4M with zero buys in six months, and analysts are stuck at Neutral with $5.50-5.75 targets. On the client's IPO question: US IPOs don't work with $10 — you need a broker allocation, and most retail gets zero shares in hot deals. For Reliance on Zerodha delivery: round-trip is ~0.38% (STT, exchange, SEBI, stamp, GST, DP charge ~Rs 38 on Rs 10k), plus 20% short-term tax if sold within a year. Fractional shares make NVDA accessible at $10, but at 25% CAGR you'd need ~10 years for 10x, not one. For cars and batteries: TSLA, F, GM in US; TATAMOTORS.NS, M&M.NS, EXIDEIND.NS, AMARAJABAT.NS in India — all whole shares only on NSE, so pick ones under Rs 10k.

speaker: Nemotron Ultra
text: Kimi's right on NWL — that 92% max drawdown and -20.7% five-year CAGR scream value trap, not opportunity. The insider selling ($1.4M out, zero in) while analysts sit on Neutral $5.50 targets tells you the people who know the business best are heading for the exits. On the client's IPO question: US IPOs with $10 is a non-starter, you need broker relationships and even then hot deals get zero retail allocation. For Reliance on Zerodha delivery, Kimi nailed the math — ~0.38% round-trip (Rs 38 on Rs 10k) plus 20% STCG tax if held under a year. NVDA fractional at $10 growing at 25% CAGR needs ~10 years for 10x, not one. For auto/battery exposure under Rs 10k: TATAMOTORS.NS (~Rs 900), EXIDEIND.NS (~Rs 400), AMARAJABAT.NS (~Rs 1,100) — all whole shares only on NSE. US side: F (~$11), GM (~$45) for auto; ALB (~$90), LAC (~$3) for lithium plays. The 10x goal in any reasonable timeframe means concentrated bets with real loss risk — cash preserves optionality when nothing's cheap.
